# ProofForge

> ProofForge turns Meta's Muse models into provers of financial code. Each task states what financial code must guarantee as locked Lean 4 requirements. ProofForge refutes code that breaks one with a counterexample the Lean kernel checks, and accepts a fix, written by Muse Spark or by people, only when six independent kernels check its proof. Every verdict is a Passport, bound by hash to the specification, the source and the executable, that anyone can re-run.

With ProofForge as its MCP server, Muse Code, Meta's coding agent, running Muse Spark 1.3 verified 10 of 10 runs on OpenZeppelin Math.sqrt behind the Aerodrome first deposit, against 0 of 10 on its own (preregistered one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.0000054), and 2 of 10 runs on Compound Proposal 62, against 0 of 10, the first verified repairs of that task in any measured run.

Six real financial failures are specified in Lean 4: Cetus, Balancer V2, Euler Finance, Knight Capital, Hundred Finance, Compound Proposal 62. Each vulnerable version is refuted by a kernel-checked counterexample, and each has a VERIFIED repair written by Muse Spark 1.3 (with Muse Wonder 1.0 planning on Balancer V2 and Knight Capital, and in Muse Code on Compound) and checked by ProofForge. The five with a quoted dollar loss total more than $1 billion taken or lost, as the cited sources report.

Built during the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon: first commit 2026-10-26, submissions due 2026-11-04 (ORIGIN.md). Machine-readable version: /evidence.json. Source: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge

## Meta models and tools used

- Muse Code 1.4.14 (Meta's coding agent). Runs ProofForge as an MCP server (integrations/muse/proofforge_mcp.py) with the ProofForge skill (.agents/skills/proofforge/SKILL.md) and the ProofForgeFin library in its workspace; headless `muse exec` runs driven by agents/muse_code.py, every model request metered at the wire (integrations/muse/meter.py). The arm on its own is the same Muse Code with Lean only (the MCP server's `lean_build`). Results: results/frontier-2, results/frontier-3, results/hard-task-1, results/vyper-replication-1, results/muse-code-1.
- Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta Model API, Contributor tier; model ID muse-spark-1.3-contributor). The model inside Muse Code in every Muse Code run, and the repairer, implementer and prover of arms A0 (on its own), A1 (the ProofForge harness) and A2 (A1 with the Muse Wonder planner). Results: results/baseline-flagships-1, results/e1-test-1, results/library-1.
- Muse Wonder 1.0 (Meta Model API; model ID muse-wonder-1.0). The lemma planner of arm A2: when an obligation resists direct proof, it proposes helper lemma statements that Muse Spark 1.3 then proves, on one budget. Results: results/library-1, results/knight-1, results/balancer-1.
- Muse Spark Open (Meta's open-weight model on Baseten Model APIs; model ID meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026). Arms A0 and A1 on the 30 frozen E1 test tasks. Results: results/e1-test-open-1.
- Muse Glimmer 30B (self-hosted with vLLM on one Modal H100; model ID glimmer/muse-glimmer-30b). Arms A0 and A1 on the frozen E1 test tasks; incomplete when the host paused the workspace. Results: results/e1-test-glimmer-1.

## The frontier, measured: Meta's models with ProofForge

- What Meta's models reach with ProofForge that they do not reach on their own: every measured comparison of a Meta model on its own (A0 compile-and-retry, or Muse Code with Lean only) and the same model with ProofForge (A1 harness, A2 harness with the Muse Wonder 1.0 planner, or Muse Code with the ProofForge MCP server), judged by ProofForge against the same locked specification. Generated by eval/wins.py from the raw run files with no model calls; every comparison is kept, each test with its p value.
- 234 comparisons over 489 runs: on 22 the model verified only with ProofForge, on 86 it verified either way and ProofForge made it cheaper or faster, and 50 are gains of other kinds. Ledger: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/ledger.json; prose: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md; page: /frontier
- 0 → 10 of 10: OpenZeppelin Math.sqrt behind the Aerodrome first deposit, a task no measured run had verified before: Muse Spark 1.3 in Muse Code verified 10 of 10 runs with ProofForge, at $1.99 per verified run, and 0 of 10 on its own after spending $95.45. Preregistered one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.0000054. ProofForgeFin now supplies the convergence of Newton's integer square root over any number of steps and the bridge from 256-bit words to natural numbers, neither in Lean's core library; both were built after the first experiment on this task, where neither arm verified (0 of 5 and 0 of 5). Caps of $10 and 4 hours per run, list prices. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#aggregates-and-real-world-tasks
- 0 → 2 of 10: Compound Proposal 62, the COMP reward distribution, a task no measured run of any arm had verified before: Muse Spark 1.3 in Muse Code verified 2 of 10 runs with ProofForge, at $42.72 per verified run, and 0 of 10 on its own after spending $92.47. Both verified runs prove the three bounds over any sequence of operations (rewards, each account, no backdated rewards) that no earlier run of either arm proved. Passports b7aca6c04101c9fc, 4f7e8adfccefae85. Preregistered one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.24; with the runs on its own of frontier-2 pooled, 2 of 10 against 0 of 20, p = 0.1. ProofForgeFin now supplies Accumulator.Market, two-sided reward markets bounded from one case analysis, written after the frontier-2 runs stopped at 5 of 8 requirements (0 of 10 and 0 of 10 verified). Caps of $10 and 4 hours per run, list prices. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#aggregates-and-real-world-tasks
- 10 → 14 of 15: Vyper sqrt(), CVE-2025-26622, in two preregistered experiments: Muse Spark 1.3 in Muse Code verified 14 of 15 runs with ProofForge and 10 of 15 on its own, 2.1x cheaper per verified run ($5.62 against $11.79) and 1.7x faster. First experiment 5 of 5 with ProofForge against 2 of 5; replication 9 of 10 against 8 of 10, at lower cost per run with ProofForge (preregistered one-sided Mann-Whitney U p = 0.022). ProofForgeFin supplies the error bound of Newton's method with floor division, which Lean's core library does not have. Caps of $10 and 4 hours per run, list prices. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#aggregates-and-real-world-tasks
- 6.5x cheaper: Per verified Balancer V2 repair: Muse Spark 1.3 verified 3 of 3 runs with ProofForge at $3.06 each and 2 of 5 on its own at $20.02, 1.8x faster. With ProofForge, Muse Wonder 1.0 plans the lemmas and Muse Spark 1.3 proves them: two Meta models working together on one budget. Caps of $10 and 4 hours per run, list prices; runs from three experiments. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#aggregates-and-real-world-tasks
- 6 tasks of 30: Where Muse Spark Open, Meta's open-weight model, did not verify on its own and verified with ProofForge, on the frozen test tasks; on its own, each of those 6 runs stopped at the $3 cap. Over all 30 tasks: 24 verified with ProofForge, 21 on its own. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#e1-test-open-1-per-task
- 0 of 247 vs 233: Seeded bad candidates accepted by ProofForge; ordinary checking (the build passes, the theorem names exist, the axioms are clean) accepted 233, the rebuild with property tests 1. And no false alarm: ProofForge rejected 0 of 239 good candidates. The bad candidates are the seeded attacks of the E2 suite. Full comparison: https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge/blob/main/results/wins/README.md#catches-e2-all-1
- Every comparison, by dimension, with ProofForge: verification better on 37, the same on 180, worse on 17; cost better on 101, the same on 8, worse on 91; time better on 72, the same on 9, worse on 80; requirements better on 63, the same on 151, worse on 20; cap stops better on 40, the same on 182, worse on 12.

## Cetus, 2025-05-22

- Loss: about $223 million taken, as The Block reports from Cetus's incident report. Sources: https://www.theblock.co/post/355795/sui-dex-cetus-open-source-library-flaw-smart-contract-223-million-usd-exploit, https://dedaub.com/blog/the-cetus-amm-200m-hack-how-a-flawed-overflow-check-led-to-catastrophic-loss/
- Bug: The overflow check in checked_shlw tested against a 256-bit limit instead of a 192-bit limit, so a shift that lost bits reported no overflow.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-DELTA-A-COVERS): The overflow check never loses a bit, so a deposit is always charged at least the exact amount it owes.
- Vulnerable code (Original checked_shlw): REFUTED. On the attack deposit it charges 1 unit of token A; the exact amount owed, rounded up, is 31572840708638430117170542 units. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/witnesses/buggy_original.lean. Passport b79e965381258ef8a287983b492911da0c4dc7b7437bfc538c14ad196aadfad3 (results/cetus-1/passports/original-port.json)
- Same-day hotfix (pull request 6, merged 14:37 UTC): REFUTED. It refuses the attack deposit, but checkedShlw(2^192) = (0, false): 2^192 shifted left by 64 bits wraps to 0 and no overflow is reported. A deposit with liquidity × price difference = 2^192 is charged 0. Passport d489c01595c307394d75579753303817724f7d586cffd2b7bb3b8cfe83f5e3e2 (results/cetus-1/passports/pr6-port.json)
- Final fix (pull request 7, merged 16:09 UTC): VERIFIED. All five requirements proved for every 256-bit input and every u128 price and liquidity. Passport 37d236fb45a80f418f9cfd7b63296b25c6326bb4a8517b86f8b7e806cdfa5e48 (results/cetus-1/passports/pr7-port.json)
- Muse repair: VERIFIED, 5 of 5 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; attempt 1, 428 s, 23 model calls, $0.1871 at list prices, $0.0111 charged. Passport 9131dfdfd3e27da8145cd70972c65748a5447585ce2c625dee404b1506239852 (results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json)
- Proved separately (results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/Equivalence.lean, axioms propext, Quot.sound): theorem muse_eq_pr7 : ∀ n : BitVec 256, museShlw n = pr7Shlw n
- Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean
- Real code: The real checked_shlw and get_delta_a, unmodified at each pinned commit, ran with Sui CLI 1.83.0 (sui move test) on 2,007 inputs: 7 documented values and 2,000 generated by the task oracle.
  - Original: 658 of 2007 inputs break a requirement; 2007 equal the Lean port; 1317 equal the proved repair (the attack deposit returns 1)
  - Pull request 6: 33 of 2007 inputs break a requirement; 2007 equal the Lean port; 1974 equal the proved repair (32 of them at n = 2^192)
  - Pull request 7: 0 of 2007 inputs break a requirement; 2007 equal the Lean port; 2007 equal the proved repair (identical to the Muse repair on every input)
- Not proved: The Move code is run on 2,007 inputs and compared with the Lean ports and the proved component; it is not itself proved. get_delta_b, the tick math and the rest of the pool (positions, swaps, fees) are not specified.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/README.md

## Balancer V2, 2025-11-03

- Loss: more than $120 million across Balancer and its forks, as OpenZeppelin reports; The Block reports estimates of over $128 million. Sources: https://www.openzeppelin.com/news/understanding-the-balancer-v2-exploit, https://www.theblock.co/post/377863/balancer-identifies-rounding-error-as-root-cause-of-multi-chain-defi-exploit, https://www.certora.com/blog/breaking-down-the-balancer-hack
- Bug: A swap for an exact amount out rounded that amount down before pricing it, so 17 wei of osETH, worth 17.988 of the pool's units, was priced as 17.
- Context: Certora writes that its 2022 verified properties of these pools “did not constrain the relationship between individual swaps or rounding behavior”. The locked requirements here are about exactly that.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-BATCH-KEEPS-VALUE): For any pool math meeting the stated contract, no batch of swaps of any length lowers the pool's value.
- Vulnerable code (Deployed swap path of the osETH/WETH pool): REFUTED. Four rounds of the attack's three swaps lower the pool's value from 4,749,898,000 to 297,229,191. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rw-balancer-upscale/witnesses/attack_batch.lean. Passport d65bd405a13bfd4feaef838e4cc60dea2560bc47ff78cad8dfda591aaf26cb71 (results/balancer-1/passports/port.json)
- Muse repair, planned by Muse Wonder 1.0: VERIFIED, 8 of 8 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; attempt 1, 2344 s, 151 model calls, $2.5115 at list prices, $0.4087 charged. Passport 48930efdd4d67460bfd22bb15dfa9625caafc36cd6fca3a8fee444d5f3b204ba (results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/passport.json)
- Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/passport.json --candidate results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/final.lean
- Real code: On a fork of Ethereum taken just before the attack transaction, the attack's first 22 swaps brought the deployed pool to 67,000 wei of each token, as on chain. Then 501 batches (the attack's 90 swaps and 500 generated, 10,385 swaps in all) ran through the deployed Vault, the Lean port and the Muse repair.
  - Deployed Vault and osETH/WETH pool: 56 of 501 batches break a requirement; 501 equal the Lean port; 194 equal the proved repair (the pool's invariant falls in 56 batches, and its BPT price with it)
  - Muse repair: 0 of 501 batches break a requirement (the proved component on the same 501 batches)
- Not proved: The requirements hold for any pool math meeting a stated contract; a constant-product pool is proved to meet it, StableMath is not, so results with StableMath are tested. BPT swaps, joins and exits are not modeled. The deployed contracts are run on 501 batches on a fork; they are not themselves proved.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rw-balancer-upscale/README.md

## Euler Finance, 2023-03-13

- Loss: about $197 million in net profit to the attacker, as Cyfrin reports; CoinDesk later reported that all recoverable funds were returned. Sources: https://www.cyfrin.io/blog/how-did-the-euler-finance-hack-happen-hack-analysis, https://www.zellic.io/blog/euler-finance-exploit-analysis, https://www.coindesk.com/business/2023/04/03/euler-says-all-recoverable-funds-stolen-in-200m-hack-have-been-returned
- Bug: donateToReserves moved an account's collateral to the reserves without the liquidity check that withdraw, mint and transfer perform.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-NO-BAD-DEBT): No sequence of operations leaves any account with more debt than its risk-adjusted collateral.
- Vulnerable code (Euler v1 at b1ee326): REFUTED. The attack sequence leaves 134,000,000 of debt with no collateral behind it. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rw-euler-donate/witnesses/buggy_original.lean. Passport cec7d847f1d0b6a6f9cdb0e46fd149430807f86e14ce746054484ccee3a3a050 (results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/passports/port.json)
- Muse repair: VERIFIED, 6 of 6 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; attempt 1, 1682 s, 40 model calls, $0.8324 at list prices, $0.0489 charged. Passport 6de7bb94c38cf23a31ba08174d7505b4b8d54dddc9ffbd6d177dde4981b82002 (results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/passport.json)
- Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/final.lean
- Real code: The unmodified contracts at b1ee326 were deployed in a local Foundry test and run on the attack, Euler's three donate test scenarios and 1,000 generated sequences, then compared after every operation with the requirements, with Euler's own liquidity computation and with the Muse repair.
  - Euler v1 at b1ee326, unmodified: 57 of 1004 sequences break a requirement; 947 equal the proved repair (Euler's own liquidity check also reports collateral below liability in 57)
  - The same with checkLiquidity(account) added: 0 of 1004 sequences break a requirement; 1004 equal the proved repair (a local copy, not an upstream release)
- Not proved: One asset priced at 1, an eToken exchange rate fixed at 1 and no interest; flash loans, sub-accounts and multiple collateral assets are not modeled. The contracts are run on 1,004 sequences and compared with the requirements and the proved component; they are not themselves proved.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rw-euler-donate/README.md

## Knight Capital, 2012-08-01

- Reconstructed: Knight Capital is reconstructed from the SEC's findings (Release No. 34-70694) because Knight's code is not public; nothing in the task is Knight's code, and every Knight Passport says so.
- Loss: $460 million realized loss, as the SEC order states. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2013/34-70694.pdf, https://web.archive.org/web/20201212052325/https://www.sec.gov/litigation/admin/2013/34-70694.pdf
- Bug: New code was not copied to one of eight servers. There, orders carrying a repurposed flag ran dead Power Peg code, which kept sending child orders without counting the executions.
- Context: The SEC order reports millions of child orders for 212 parent orders: 4 million executions in 154 stocks, more than 397 million shares, in about 45 minutes.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-NEVER-OVERROUTE): On every server and code version, after any sequence of events, the shares sent for an order never exceed its quantity.
- Vulnerable code (Reconstructed Power Peg router): REFUTED. For every n, n rounds of a 100-share routing opportunity and a fill send n child orders and 100 × n shares for one 100-share order. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rc-knight-router/witnesses/buggy_original.lean. Passport ca3e7312fe7af22f53f52fbd08f53dfc85bde86ebe49a96e0e9751e4f365a6b8 (results/knight-1/start/passport.json)
- Muse repair, planned by Muse Wonder 1.0: VERIFIED, 6 of 6 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; attempt 2, 4079 s, 256 model calls, $4.96 at list prices, $0.9788 charged. Passport 98cfed64ae1ec596e517299b422a5fb0beac571cdce89c18ea2e5660845bc178 (results/knight-1/A2-2/passport.json)
- Earlier attempt A1, attempt 1: UNRESOLVED; its executable passed all 2001 property cases, but it proved 1 of 6 requirements before its wall-clock cap, so no VERIFIED Passport. Passport 4fddc1683956e92f1f0a7e97eb48bdc238e233b55b9e430dda47062bfaac5e74 (results/knight-1/A1-1/passport.json)
- Earlier attempt A1, attempt 2: UNRESOLVED; its executable passed all 2001 property cases, but it proved 1 of 6 requirements before its dollar cap, so no VERIFIED Passport. Passport 27f4c83221ed220ea8e52e955a82a45bd73f9d8eed2d0136081096a4b09afb6c (results/knight-1/A1-2/passport.json)
- Earlier attempt A2, attempt 1: UNRESOLVED; its executable passed all 2001 property cases, but it proved 5 of 6 requirements before its dollar cap, so no VERIFIED Passport. Passport edc4ec8cd40a2db0fb8b77a2c959e5d9e4cb236403e5ce4e3cb2778bd5279c9b (results/knight-1/A2-1/passport.json)
- Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/knight-1/A2-2/passport.json --candidate results/knight-1/A2-2/final.lean
- Real code: none: the code is not public
- Not proved: The mechanism by which fills stopped reaching Power Peg's count is one interpretation of paragraphs 14 and 16 of the order; other mechanisms with the same outcome are possible. Prices, venues, order types, timing and cancellations are not modeled. The executable wrapper is tested, not proved.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rc-knight-router/README.md

## Hundred Finance, 2023-04-15

- Loss: about $7 million in reported losses (rekt.news gives $7.4M; this figure was not checked here). Sources: https://rekt.news/hundred-rekt2, https://blocksec.com/blog/6-hundred-finance-incident-catalyzing-the-wave-of-precision-related-exploits-in-vulnerable-forked-protocols
- Bug: redeemUnderlying rounded the shares burned down, so a withdrawal worth 1.99999999992 share units burned 1.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-SHARE-VALUE): No sequence of operations, donations included, lowers the value of a share while shares are outstanding.
- Vulnerable code (Hundred hToken share accounting): REFUTED. After the attack's own amounts, the last share unit is backed by 2 satoshi. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rw-hundred-vault/witnesses/hundred_attack.lean
- Muse repair: VERIFIED, 10 of 10 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; attempt 1, 1200 s, 67 model calls, $0.6513 at list prices, $0.037 charged. Passport 08fe86f17f27c49d60bda786d1498200d333c1c8d63d2f858ab668cd4f7fe7c4 (results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json)
- Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean
- Real code: On a fork of Optimism at block 90761917, the hWBTC market was emptied as in the attack, and 501 sequences (the attack and 500 generated) ran on the deployed CErc20Delegate bytecode, on the Lean port and on the Muse repair.
  - Deployed hWBTC contract: 292 of 501 sequences break a requirement; 501 equal the Lean port; 209 equal the proved repair (identical to the Lean port after every operation of all 501)
  - Muse repair: 0 of 501 sequences break a requirement (the proved component, on the same 501 sequences)
- Not proved: Only share accounting is modeled; the comptroller, borrowing, liquidation, interest and reserves are not. The specification states the share-value property the borrow relied on. The deployed contract is run on 501 sequences on a fork and compared with the port and the requirements; it is not itself proved.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rw-hundred-vault/README.md

## Compound Proposal 62, 2021-09-29

- Loss: at worst 280,000 COMP, about $80 million at the time, as The Block reports, quoting Robert Leshner; not included in the loss total. Sources: https://www.theblock.co/post/119086/compound-bug-comp-risk-misreward, https://compound.substack.com/p/compound-treasury-updates-comp-bug
- Bug: The upgrade set every reward index still at 0 to compInitialIndex (1e36), but distributeSupplierComp and distributeBorrowerComp started an account with no recorded index from compInitialIndex only when the market's index was above it (>), so in six markets an account holding a position from before the upgrade was credited from 0: about one COMP per token borrowed. Proposal 64 changed > to >=.
- Property proved in Lean 4 (REQ-REWARDS-BOUNDED): From the upgrade of any well-formed pre-upgrade state, after any sequence of operations, the COMP paid out to accounts plus the COMP accrued to them never exceeds what they held or had accrued before the upgrade, plus what they were owed at the upgrade, plus the COMP emitted since.
- Vulnerable code (Proposal 62 port): REFUTED, 5 of 8 requirements refuted. The cSUSHI claim made on mainnet 139 blocks after the upgrade: nothing was owed and nothing was emitted to the market, and the port pays 18977306140567618322762 COMP-wei (18,977.35 COMP), as the transaction did. Kernel-checked counterexample: realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/witnesses/cSUSHI_claim.lean. Passport 3ac121be0f5748feeb430e95637d409048441b55a91e009b2253f3ded07693a3 (results/compound-1/passports/port.json)
- Muse repair in Muse Code with ProofForge (results/frontier-3/README.md): 2 of 10 runs VERIFIED, 0 of 10 on its own (0 of 20 with frontier-2 pooled); one-sided Fisher exact p = 0.24, pooled p = 0.1.
  - results/frontier-3 proofforge-full-5: VERIFIED, 8 of 8 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; Muse Code 1.4.14 (1.4.14-R7309.1), muse-spark-1.3-contributor, MCP profile full, ended at an accepted check, 2953 s, 305 model calls, $6.70 at list prices, $0.1972 charged. Passport b7aca6c04101c9fc27a6baca82e45dddaf69663c698f95913434c354e97e2beb (results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-5/passport.json). Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-5/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-3/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-5/final.lean
  - results/frontier-3 proofforge-full-9: VERIFIED, 8 of 8 requirements, 6 kernels, 2001 property cases; Muse Code 1.4.14 (1.4.14-R7309.1), muse-spark-1.3-contributor, MCP profile full, ended at an accepted check, 1119 s, 230 model calls, $7.41 at list prices, $0.2601 charged. Passport 4f7e8adfccefae8542370f3a9621b72594978fc2166283f4f000eefc9aabfb1e (results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-9/passport.json). Reproduce: bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-9/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-3/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-9/final.lean
- Before frontier-3 no measured run of any method verified the task (results/frontier-3/README.md): Muse Spark 1.3 alone (A0) 0 of 4, with the ProofForge harness (A1) 0 of 2, with the harness and the Muse Wonder planner 0 of 7, implement mode 0 of 2, and Muse Code in frontier-2 0 of 10 on its own and 0 of 10 with ProofForge.
- Proposal 64 fix, ported by the build team: VERIFIED, 8 of 8 requirements. Passport 7ccce9a2ebe8bffb61198e010b595f3126fb0ac5aa21c9906fe73593b2528d4a (results/compound-1/passports/reference.json)
- Real code: Comptrollers compiled from the pinned commits with solc 0.5.16 (identical to the deployed runtime code, metadata hash excluded) ran in Foundry on 503 sequences: the cSUSHI claim, Compound's regression scenario, the Sanity sequence and 500 generated.
  - Proposal 62: 279 of 503 sequences break a requirement (identical to the Lean port on all 503)
  - Proposal 64: 104 of 503 sequences break a requirement (REQ-CLAIM only, its temporary claim lock; identical to its Lean port on all 503)
  - Proposal 65: 0 of 503 sequences break a requirement (identical to the proved component on all 503)
- Not proved: The Solidity contracts are not proved; they were compiled from the pinned commits, run on the sequences above and compared operation by operation with the port and the proved component. The specification covers one market; it does not cover several markets sharing compAccrued, the oracle and liquidity checks of the hooks, interest accrual or the Proposal 65 corrections.
- Task: realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/README.md

## Muse alone and Muse with ProofForge

- Every run is Muse Spark 1.3 (Contributor tier), capped at $10 at list prices and 14400 s, and judged by ProofForge against the same locked specification. A0: Muse alone, compile-and-retry with Lean's errors and the axiom audit. A1: the ProofForge harness. A2: A1 with Muse Wonder 1.0 as lemma planner. On Cetus, Euler and Hundred both Muse alone and the harness were accepted in every run. On Balancer and Knight, A2 was accepted more often and at a lower list price per verified run than Muse alone (cost_per_verified_run). On Compound, Muse Code (Muse Spark 1.3) with ProofForge verified 2 of 10 runs in frontier-3 (results/frontier-3/README.md), the first verified repairs of the task; on its own it verified 0 of 10, and 0 of 20 with frontier-2 pooled. Before frontier-3 no run of any method had proved every Compound requirement (the rows below); the build team's library-based proof is VERIFIED on the deployed judge.
- Cetus (rw-cetus-shlw): Muse alone accepted 2 of 2; A1 1 of 1; implement mode 1 of 1; vulnerable code refuted on 2 of 2 requirements (original code) by kernel-checked counterexamples and 1 of 1 requirements (same-day hotfix) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Euler Finance (rw-euler-donate): Muse alone accepted 2 of 2; A1 1 of 1; implement mode 1 of 1; vulnerable code refuted on 3 of 3 requirements (vulnerable port) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Hundred Finance (rw-hundred-vault): Muse alone accepted 2 of 2; A1 1 of 1; implement mode 1 of 1; vulnerable code refuted on 2 of 5 requirements (vulnerable port) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Balancer V2 (rw-balancer-upscale): Muse alone accepted 1 of 2; A1 1 of 2, A2 1 of 1; implement mode 1 of 2; vulnerable code refuted on 3 of 3 requirements (deployed swap path) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Knight Capital (rc-knight-router): Muse alone accepted 1 of 2; A1 0 of 2, A2 1 of 2; implement mode 1 of 1; vulnerable code refuted on 6 of 6 requirements (reconstructed router) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Compound Proposal 62 (rw-compound-comp): Muse alone accepted 0 of 2; A1 0 of 2, A2 0 of 2; implement mode 0 of 2; vulnerable code refuted on 5 of 5 requirements (Proposal 62 port) by kernel-checked counterexamples.
- Balancer V2 over all measured runs, including results/library-1: Muse alone 2 of 5; with the Muse Wonder planner 3 of 3.
- Knight Capital over all measured runs, including results/library-1: Muse alone 1 of 2; with the Muse Wonder planner 3 of 4.
- Compound Proposal 62 over all measured runs, including results/library-1: Muse alone 0 of 4; with the Muse Wonder planner 0 of 7.
- Balancer, list price per verified run: $3.06 with ProofForge and the Muse Wonder planner (3 of 3 verified), $20.02 for Muse on its own (2 of 5). One-sided Fisher exact p = 0.18 on the rate.
- Knight Capital, list price per verified run: $8.85 with ProofForge and the Muse Wonder planner (3 of 4 verified), $16.22 for Muse on its own (1 of 2). One-sided Fisher exact p = 0.6 on the rate.
- Specification strength (results/spec-strength-1, docs/SPEC_STRENGTH.md): the 25 locked specifications reject 999 of 1114 compiling single-site mutants of their reference solutions, 730 with kernel-checked counterexamples; 10 surviving mutants behave differently and are reported as specification gaps.
- Counterexamples (results/counterexamples-1/summary.json): 82 of 85 refuted requirements over 33 candidates refuted by a Lean theorem accepted by six kernels and leanchecker. The Cetus same-day hotfix: ¬ (ShlwExact checkedShlw) at n = 6277101735386680763835789423207666416102355444464034512896 (2^192).
- Muse Spark Open (meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026 on Baseten Model APIs; results/e1-test-open-1/e1.json): A0 21 of 30, A1 24 of 30; McNemar p = 0.51, 95% interval of the difference [-0.172, 0.379].
- Muse Glimmer 30B (self-hosted with vLLM on one Modal H100; results/e1-test-glimmer-1/e1.json, incomplete): A0 0 of 15, A1 3 of 13 excluding runs ended by an outage (3 of 16 including them); McNemar p = 0.25, 95% interval of the difference [0, 0.389].
- Muse Wonder planner on Compound: A1 proved 0 and 0 of 8 requirements, A2 5 and 5; A2 accepted in 0 of 2.
- Muse Wonder planner on Knight Capital: A1 proved 1 and 1 of 6 requirements, A2 5 and 6; A2 accepted in 1 of 2.
- ProofForgeFin (lib/): 2051 theorems and 478 definitions in 82 files; 10909 safe constants of the library and demonstrations accepted by six kernels in the latest full run (lib/README.md); the last committed full run (results/feedback-library-1/kernels-full.json) checked 10128 and leanchecker replayed 87 modules. A library-based Compound candidate written by the build team (tests/fixtures/library/compound_lib.lean) is VERIFIED on the deployed judge, Passport b654d456e1a5eec1057ee259be2c2726fee3a4d3b89d1373dcc3bcbf1c4b7f59 (results/library-live-1/passport.json).
- Scope: ProofForge proves the logic of code against a written specification. It does not protect keys, servers, oracles, bridges or other infrastructure, and it does not prove the deployed Solidity or Move bytecode itself.

## Benchmark

- 59 repair tasks in six families: payouts (9), ledgers (10), transfer batches (10), permissions (10), rate limiters (10), queues (10); 23 development, 6 validation, 30 test.
- E1 (results/e1-test-1/e1.json): on the 30 frozen test tasks, A0 Compile-and-retry completed 28, A1 ProofForge harness completed 30, A2 Harness and planner completed 30; McNemar exact p = 0.5 against A0. 90 runs cost $70.09 at list prices.
- E2 (results/e2-all-1/e2.json): seeded bad repairs accepted, out of 247: Ordinary checking 233, Rebuild and property tests only 1, ProofForge 0. Correct repairs rejected, out of 239: Ordinary checking 0, Rebuild and property tests only 0, ProofForge 0. Every bad case is a seeded attack written by the build team.

## Not claimed

- The deployed Solidity and Move code is not itself proved. Each incident's Lean 4 port is a reviewed hand translation, tested against the real code on the stated inputs; the translation is not machine-checked.
- A requirement covers exactly what its Lean statement says. Each port models only the logic named in its task README.
- Loss figures are quoted from the sources each task README cites.
- The JSON wrapper around each proved function is tested, not proved.
- Knight Capital is reconstructed from the SEC's findings (Release No. 34-70694) because Knight's code is not public; nothing in the task is Knight's code, and every Knight Passport says so.

## Reproduce

    git clone https://github.com/davidwilliam/proof_forge && cd proof_forge
    docker build -t proofforge-lean:4.35.0 -f infra/docker/Dockerfile.lean infra/docker
    bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/original-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/buggy_original.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/cetus-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/pr6-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/attacks/pr6_mask_only.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/cetus-1/passports/pr7-port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-cetus-shlw/reference/SolutionA.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-balancer-upscale/attacks/balancer_port.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/passport.json --candidate results/balancer-1/repair-A2-1/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-euler-donate/candidate/Solution.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/euler-1/rw-euler-donate/repair-A1-1/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/knight-1/start/passport.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rc-knight-router/candidate/Solution.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/knight-1/A2-2/passport.json --candidate results/knight-1/A2-2/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/passport.json --candidate results/vault-1/repair-A1-1/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/compound-1/passports/port.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/attacks/p62_port.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-5/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-3/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-5/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/frontier-3/judged/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-9/passport.json --candidate results/frontier-3/runs/rw-compound-comp/proofforge-full-9/final.lean
    bin/proofforge verify results/compound-1/passports/reference.json --candidate realworld/tasks/rw-compound-comp/reference/SolutionA.lean

## Pages

- /: overview with the measured gains of Meta's models with ProofForge and the six real failures
- /frontier: what Meta's models reach with ProofForge that they do not reach on their own, and every comparison
- /#check: check a fix; submits a real-world candidate to POST /api/verify on the API, with the committed Passport as fallback
- /app: the Balancer V2 rounding exploit replayed on the deployed swap code, the plus-one hotfix and the repair Muse proved with ProofForge
- /challenge: hidden payout variants checked by the property tests derived from the locked requirements, each violation with a concrete witness
- /forge: live forge session (replay of a recorded Muse repair, then a fresh check)
- /passport/{sha256}: one Passport, with its per-requirement statuses, hashes and reproduction command
- /results: E1 and E2 per arm, family and case
- /methods: every preregistered experiment, with its question, commit, run count, primary test, status and result
- /verify: the commands that reproduce a Passport and what bin/proofforge verify compares
- /brand: the identity kit, with the palette, the rules and every file to download
- /about: who built ProofForge, why, what was built during the hackathon, and acknowledgments
